python/cudf_polars/cudf_polars/dsl/expressions/unary.py: 1

`1918-1934`: ** Trivial** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Quick win** **Reuse the NaN masks in the restore loop.** The float path computes each mask twice. It also copies each mask through `replace_nulls`, although `is_nan` returns a non-nullable mask. This adds full-column GPU work for every input column. Reuse the masks and keep the original NaN values during restoration.
Suggested fix

Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Directly linked issue `#24988` requires cudf-polars max_horizontal to ignore NaN when a row also has a non-NaN value, as Polars does. It also asks that min_horizontal be checked for the same behavior. No other linked issue applies. Implementation at reviewed head (python/cudf_polars/cudf_polars/dsl/expressions/unary.py, UnaryFunction.do_evaluate, horizontal fold branch, whole-PR diff against merge base): - For floating-point output dtypes, each input column is masked. NaN values become null through copy_if_else with a null scalar, using mask = replace_nulls(is_nan(col), False). The existing NULL_MAX/NULL_MIN fold then skips NaN, as Polars does. - After the fold, for each original column, rows whose folded result is null and whose input is NaN are set to NaN. Rows with only nulls stay null. The first NaN input sets the result, and later columns do not overwrite it, because they test is_null(result). - The same branch covers min_horizontal through _horizontal_fold_ops, so the fix applies to both functions. - Non-floating dtypes skip the new code and use the previous path. Tests at reviewed head (python/cudf_polars/tests/expressions/test_horizontal.py, test_minmax_horizontal_skips_nan, parametrized over max and min): three columns and seven rows cover all-NaN rows, NaN with null, all-null rows, and mixed finite values. The test compares GPU and CPU output through assert_gpu_result_equal. I checked the expected behavior of each row against the code logic. It matches. Uncertainty: the incremental diff from the previous reviewed head (ab3dd61) could not be read, because changed blobs are missing from the checkout. This verdict uses the whole-PR diff against merge base 16c0014 and the file content at head. I did not run the test suite. The is_nan call runs on every input column. For a horizontal call that mixes a non-floating input with a floating output dtype, behavior depends on libcudf is_nan handling of that dtype. No test covers that case. I did not find evidence that Polars passes such mixed inputs to this branch, so this does not change the verdict.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The whole-PR diff (merge base 16c0014 to head 2e6e63d) changes two files in the reviewed scope: - python/cudf_polars/cudf_polars/dsl/expressions/unary.py: NaN masking and NaN restore inside the horizontal fold branch. The branch applies only to max_horizontal and min_horizontal, and only to floating-point output dtypes. - python/cudf_polars/tests/expressions/test_horizontal.py: one parametrized regression test, test_minmax_horizontal_skips_nan, for max_horizontal and min_horizontal. Both changes connect directly to `#24988`. The comparison logic for NULL_MAX and NULL_MIN is not changed, which matches the PR description and the exclusion of the `#18842` behavior. No unrelated refactoring, configuration, or documentation changes appear in the changed files. The incremental diff from the previous reviewed head could not be read, so this verdict relies on the whole-PR diff and the file content at head.
